title: Telemetry MVP scope prioritization and intentional cuts for Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Define a minimal, shippable telemetry surface for Redwood Console focused on dashboards, traces, and cost breakdowns while making pragmatic cuts to meet an April launch window. This ticket captures scope decisions, acceptance criteria, implementation constraints, and follow-ups for deferred features.
scope_summary: Deliver a read-only Console telemetry MVP that provides: 1) per-route latency and error dashboards with two selectable time windows (1h, 24h), 2) lightweight tracing linking slow requests to model variant and region, and 3) a simplified cost breakdown by route and model (daily totals). Intentionally exclude advanced features: per-token cost drilling, synthetic span generation, long-term storage (>90 days), multi-tenant RBAC for telemetry, and automated alerting in MVP.
scope_cuts_and_rationale: Cut: Per-token and per-token-step cost drilldowns. Rationale: high engineering complexity and backend storage costs; low immediate customer usage for MVP.

Cut: Synthetic tracing spans / automatic span enrichment. Rationale: Significant runtime instrumentation changes required and increased trace volume; can be scheduled for post-MVP tracing quality sprint.
Cut: Alerting and on-console policy rules. Rationale: Requires stable signal definitions and incident playbooks; postpone until after basic dashboards validated.
Cut: Model-level historical QoE regression alerts. Rationale: Needs evaluation harness and baseline metrics; out of MVP scope.
Cut: >90 day retention and cold-storage export UI. Rationale: Storage and compliance decisions deferred to Dedicated/Private roadmap.
Cut: Fine-grained RBAC controls for telemetry views. Rationale: MVP will reuse existing Console RBAC roles; dedicated telemetry RBAC to follow.
Kept: Two time-window dashboard view (1h, 24h). Rationale: Provides immediate surface area for latency spikes and trends with minimal UI complexity.
Kept: Trace sampling at 1% by default with an opt-in toggle at org level. Rationale: Minimizes trace volume while enabling root-cause for latency regressions.
Kept: Cost breakdown aggregated by route and model per day. Rationale: Provides customers with actionable unit economics without heavy cardinality.
Kept: Link from a slow latency dashboard row to a representative trace (when available). Rationale: Small UX win for troubleshooting.
Kept: Read-only initial release. Rationale: Simplifies security and rollout; will add edit/alert features in follow-ups.
tradeoffs: Sampling traces reduces visibility for tail latency root-cause but keeps storage and ingestion budgets acceptable for MVP.
Aggregating cost by day and by route reduces granularity for cost attribution but dramatically lowers storage and query complexity.
Delaying alerting reduces operational readiness for customers but allows us to validate metrics and traces without producing noisy or misconfigured alerts.
Reusing existing RBAC accelerates shipping but defers enterprise-specific access controls, which some customers will request promptly after launch.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: A per-route dashboard accessible from Console nav showing latency P50/P95/P99, request rate, error rate for 1h and 24h windows.
Dashboards: Dashboard rows are linkable and open a panel with sample request distribution and top-3 contributing model variants.
Tracing: Tracing UI surface that can display sampled traces and shows model variant, region, request id, and timeline for spans when available.
Tracing: Default trace sample rate is 1%; org admin can edit sample rate via a single toggle in the telemetry settings page.
Cost: Cost breakdown page that surfaces daily cost per route and per model aggregated across the selected window, downloadable as CSV.
Performance: Dashboard queries must return within 1.5s for common 24h queries under staging dataset load; API endpoints must meet existing Console SLOs.
Docs: Updated Console docs with MVP telemetry feature guide, limitations, and a migration note listing deferred capabilities.
E2E: Smoke test linking a high-latency request (simulated) to a trace visible in Console during staging runbook.
Security: No new telemetry-specific roles created in MVP; verify existing RBAC prevents unauthorized write actions (read-only surface).
implementation_notes: Backend: Use aggregated metrics pipeline (existing metrics buckets) to populate latency and error rate widgets to avoid building a new rollup layer.
Backend: Store cost aggregates at daily granularity keyed by (org, route, model_variant) to bound cardinality.
Tracing: Integrate with current tracing ingestion; enable 1% sampling at ingest; add a light-weight trace index for Console lookups.
UI: Use existing Console chart components and table patterns; avoid building custom visualizations for MVP.
Operational: Route telemetry feature flag behind 'telemetry-ui-mvp' for staged rollout and quick rollback.
open_questions: Q1: Do we accept a default 1% trace sample across all customers or should high-tier customers get 10% by default? (needs legal/biz input for cost implications)
Q2: Should cost CSV export include estimated token counts or just USD cost? (engineering cost for token attribution is non-trivial)
Q3: What is acceptable retention for sampled traces in the MVP environment (30/60/90 days)? Current recommendation: 30 days for staging and 60 days for prod trial.
Q4: Are there any compliance constraints from existing enterprise contracts that would block sending traces to hosted telemetry?
decisions: D1: Finalized scope cuts list on 2026-02-18 after design/eng triage — removed per-token drilldowns and alerting from MVP.
D2: Trace sampling set to 1% by default with an org-level toggle; high-tier override deferred to Post-MVP roadmap.
D3: Cost breakdown will be daily-aggregated USD totals; token-level estimates postponed.
D4: MVP will be read-only; write paths for alerting and policy controls will land in subsequent releases.
